jobs.title: Director, Data and Insights
jobs.description:
At Pacific Blue Cross, we're committed to improving health and wellbeing for British Columbians. As our Director, Data & Insights Office, you'll have a rare opportunity to build and shape a critical enterprise capability that will influence how decisions are made across the organization for years to come.

Reporting to the Vice President, Information Technology & Enterprise Transformation, you will lead the development of PBC's enterprise data, analytics, and AI strategy, helping transform data from an operational asset into a strategic advantage. Working closely with executive leaders and business partners, you will establish the foundations that enable trusted insights, stronger decision-making, and greater organizational agility.

This is more than a data leadership role. It is an opportunity to drive meaningful transformation across the organization. You'll influence enterprise priorities, champion innovation, and create a culture where data empowers teams to better serve members, improve operational performance, and deliver on PBC's long-term strategic objectives.

We're looking for a strategic and collaborative leader who is energized by building new capabilities, navigating complexity, and creating lasting organizational impact. You bring the vision to define what's possible, the influence to bring people together, and the execution focus to turn strategy into measurable results.

If your experience includes roles such as Director of Data & Analytics, Director of Business Intelligence, Head of Data & Insights, Director of Data Governance, Director of Enterprise Analytics, Director of Data Strategy, Director of AI & Analytics, Chief Data Officer, Analytics Director, Enterprise Data Leader, or similar leadership positions, and you've successfully leveraged data, analytics, and emerging technologies to drive business outcomes within industries such as healthcare, insurance, financial services, telecommunications, consulting, retail, or other complex, data-driven environments

Key Details

Position Title: Director, Data and Insights
Work Arrangement: Hybrid - 3 days in the office and 2 days’ work from home
Office Location: 4250 Canada Way, Burnaby, BC V5G 4W6
Classification: Exempt
Salary Range: $138,000 - $208,000 ( Pacific Blue Cross’ compensation program is built on a pay-for-performance philosophy, rewarding both individual and organizational achievements. We determine starting salaries by considering a variety of factors, including relevant skills, education, experience, and internal equity, ensuring compensation decisions are consistent, equitable, and reflective of each candidate’s unique background and qualifications)
Incentive Compensation Plan (ICP bonus) per year based on performance: Up to 15.00%

Total Rewards Highlights:

Flexible working hours of 7.5 hours per day, Monday to Friday (i.e., 37.5 hours per week).
Paid vacation starts at 4 weeks per year and increases with years of service.
Generous benefits, including extended health, dental, and life insurance; depending on the plan that you choose, these benefit premiums can be 100% paid by PBC.
PBC contributes the equivalent of 8% of your base salary to a Defined Contribution pension plan. No employee contribution or matching is required, giving you more take-home pay

About Pacific Blue Cross

Pacific Blue Cross (PBC) has been British Columbia’s leading benefits provider for over 80 years. We are an independent, not-for-profit society with strong roots in BC’s health care system.

Why You'll Love Working Here

Retiree Benefits plan that is available to employees who have at least 10 years of service with PBC and have reached the age of 55.
Access to an onsite fitness center and cafeteria, along with employee events and activities designed to foster a collaborative and engaging work environment.
Access to virtual doctors/counsellors 24/7 via our Employee Family Assistance Program!
Learning and development opportunities
Wellness initiatives and onsite amenities

In This Position, You Will:

Drive enterprise data strategy and modernization initiatives, helping advance data quality, reporting consistency, analytics capabilities, and AI readiness across business and technology teams.
Enable data-driven decision-making by improving access to trusted information, empowering leaders with actionable insights, and expanding self-service analytics capabilities.
Champion analytics and AI innovation, identifying high-value opportunities that improve operational effectiveness, enhance member experiences, and deliver measurable business value.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Data Engineer
jobs.description:
About Us

SickKids Foundation, with over 50 years of philanthropic impact is Canada's largest charitable funder of child health research, learning and care, raising over $200 million last year. As a national charity, SickKids Foundation invests in national and international initiatives to benefit children in Canada and around the world. As the fundraising partner to The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids), we are aligned in supporting Precision Child Health (PCH), the future of tailoring medicine to each child's unique traits so SickKids can diagnose faster, treat smarter, and predict better.

We are driven by our core values of integrity, collaboration, excellence, innovation, and inclusion, with goals of delivering a superior donor experience, investing in our people and culture, driving innovative and sustainable fundraising, and disrupting the market through data and technology.

SickKids Foundation is committed to an inclusive culture by embedding equity, diversity and inclusion in our policies, practices, and behaviours. We aim to build awareness and skills in this area, both internally and with our partners. Our commitment extends to creating a safe, positive work environment. For details on our Equity, Diversity & Inclusion commitment, please click here.

We’re committed to attracting and retaining passionate individuals to help create a healthier future. That’s why SickKids Foundation is looking for a new Associate Director, Data Engineer.

Description Of The Position

Reporting to the Director, Data Science & Engineering, the Associate Director, Data Engineer designs, builds, and operates enterprise-grade data platforms that deliver trusted, well-governed data across SickKids Foundation. The role will help establish and evolve a production-grade cloud platform using medallion architecture principles, with a focus on reliability, data quality, cost efficiency, and scalable delivery.

As a senior hands-on technical contributor, you will set engineering standards, support platform incident response, enable self-serve analytics and AI-powered data products, and provide specialized technical guidance to data and analytics partners across the Foundation.

You will

Design, build, and operate enterprise-grade data engineering platforms using modern cloud technologies such as Microsoft Fabric, Snowflake, and Databricks, aligned to bronze, silver, and gold medallion architecture principles.
Build and maintain robust, idempotent ETL/ELT pipelines with embedded validation, data quality checks, clear lineage, and repeatable delivery workflows.
Design data models and semantic layers that make trusted data accessible for analytics, reporting, and self-serve business intelligence.
Establish platform observability through query profiling, cost attribution, utilization metrics, alerting, and SLO/SLA monitoring; lead day-to-day response to data availability and performance incidents.
Define and enforce coding standards, CI/CD patterns, and Infrastructure-as-Code practices to support consistent, secure, and scalable platform deployment.
Partner with business stakeholders, Data & Analytics, IT/Infrastructure, and Security teams to translate requirements into reliable platform capabilities and support appropriate access, governance, and compliance.
Enable AI and advanced analytics use cases, including natural-language querying and AI-powered data products, by partnering with stakeholders to identify and deliver high-value opportunities.
Stay current with developments in cloud data platforms, AI, and emerging engineering practices, bringing relevant advancements into the platform roadmap and providing technical guidance to analysts, BI developers, and engineering partners.

Qualifications

While we know that for any job posting no one candidate will possess the qualifications being sought in equal measure, below is an outline of the qualifications we believe are important for a candidate to bring to the position or for the successful candidate to develop while in the role:

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
5-7 years of hands-on data engineering or platform engineering experience, ideally spanning the full lifecycle of architecting, building, and operating production data platforms.
Deep technical expertise with modern cloud data platforms such as Microsoft Fabric, Snowflake, or Databricks and strong knowledge of medallion/lakehouse architecture.
Strong data modelling and database design skills for analytics and business consumption, including dimensional modelling and semantic layers for self-serve BI.
Hands-on experience developing production-grade ETL/ELT pipelines and working with data quality, governance, CI/CD, and Infrastructure-as-Code practices.
Experience establishing observability, performance monitoring, reliability standards, and incident-response practices in production data environments.
Working knowledge of AI and advanced analytics tooling, including approaches that support natural-language querying and AI-powered data products.
Strong technical judgment, problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical stakeholder groups.
Knowledge of foundational data domains, business processes, and enterprise applications is an asset.

We’re looking for a passionate individual who is interested in moving the dial and making a difference. We are an environment that looks to attract hardworking and committed people; people who want to challenge themselves and grow with a globally recognized brand that continues to change the world. If this describes you, consider joining our team. We look forward to reviewing your application.

Total Compensation Package

Expected Hiring Salary Range:
$99,297 - $124,121; with the ability to progress to a maximum of $142,739 with demonstrated experience and proficiency. To ensure fair and equitable pay at SickKids Foundation, placement on the salary range will be based on your years of experience, skills, and qualifications relevant to the Associate Director, Data Engineer role.

To help you lead in the fight for kids’ health and to support your health, wellness, and career growth, in addition to competitive compensation, we offer a comprehensive benefit package (includes a flex benefit plan), tuition reimbursement, flexible work arrangements, pension plan and birth parent/parental top up – to name a few!

Position Status:
Permanent Full-Time.

Hours:
Hybrid work model: minimum two days per week in-office (Tuesday and Wednesday).

Available To:
Internal and External Candidates

Available
: Immediately; this posting is for an existing vacancy.

Date Posted:
October 5, 2026

Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis. We encourage interested candidates to apply early.

How to apply
: Please apply on-line by visiting our website: https://www.sickkidsfoundation.com/careersandvolunteers

Please note that automated tools, including artificial intelligence, may be used to support the pre-screening of applications as part of our recruitment process.

SickKids Foundation is committed to its people and the talents, capabilities, and perspectives they bring to our mission. We live that commitment by being open and accessible to all, by valuing and respecting every individual, and by equally supporting every employee. As an organization proud to have joined the BlackNorth Initiative’s CEO pledge, we uphold our commitment by inviting and encouraging individuals from diverse lived experiences from Black, Indigenous, communities of colour, people with disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ community and all candidates who may contribute to the further diversification of the Foundation’s community.

Candidates who require accommodation during the recruitment process should contact the People & Culture team at: recruitment@sickkidsfoundation.com

jobs.title: Senior Director, Group Product Owner - Enterprise Governance, Risk & Compliance (eGRC)
jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You'll Be Doing

As Senior Director, Group Product Owner – Enterprise Governance, Risk & Compliance (eGRC), you'll shape how CIBC identifies, manages, and responds to operational risk. You will shift our programs from manual, periodic, judgment-based activities to connected, AI-enabled capabilities that anticipate risk, automate routine work, and focus people on the decisions that matter most.

You will lead CIBC's eGRC ecosystem, including the Operational Risk System (ORS) and enterprise operational risk data governance. With a mandate to rethink, not simply maintain, you'll define the target operating model, investment priorities, and product roadmap; simplify and automate risk work with our program team; and use connected data, advanced analytics, generative and agentic AI, and continuous monitoring to surface emerging risk and improve decisions. You will ensure these capabilities are deployed responsibly through strong data, model, security, privacy, control, and human-in-the-loop practices.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You'll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you'll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You'll Succeed

Enterprise Strategy and Transformation - Define the ambition, target operating model, and multi-year roadmap for CIBC's eGRC ecosystem. Align partners and investment to the highest risk and regulatory priorities, making bold, evidence-based choices that create lasting value.
Enterprise Product Leadership - Set priorities from discovery through adoption and continuous improvement. Establish disciplined governance, translate strategy into a clear roadmap, and use customer, risk, operational, and financial insight to accelerate outcomes and demonstrate value.
Reimagining Operational Risk Programs - Redesign core programs, including risk and control assessments, control management, issues, incidents, losses, scenarios, regulatory change, and reporting. Replace fragmented manual processes with simpler, automated, connected experiences that improve coverage, reduce administration, and focus attention on the highest-risk exposures and actions.
AI, Automation and Insight-Driven Risk - Make operational risk data a trusted enterprise asset across eGRC and ORS. Set standards for ownership, quality, lineage, access, retention, and traceability; automate workflows, evidence gathering, monitoring, and reporting; and apply analytics and responsible AI to detect patterns, anticipate risk, and recommend action. Measure success through stronger outcomes, earlier intervention, better user experience, and capacity shifted from administration to judgment.
Executive Governance and Regulatory Confidence - Establish clear decision rights, accountability, and portfolio oversight. Influence senior forums with concise, forward-looking recommendations, and keep the ecosystem resilient and ready for regulatory and audit scrutiny.
Enterprise Influence and Coalition Building - Unite Business, Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit, Resilience, Third-Party, Technology, Data, and Architecture around a shared vision. Resolve trade-offs and build the executive sponsorship and cross-functional ownership needed for enterprise change.
Investment, Delivery and Strategic Partnerships - Turn ambition into an executable portfolio by aligning funding, capacity, sequencing, and risk to the highest-value outcomes. Drive performance, innovation, and measurable value while keeping eGRC and ORS stable, secure, and fit for purpose.
Leadership and Capability Building - Build a high-performing team with the product, risk, data, and transformation capabilities to lead at enterprise scale. Create clarity, empower decisions, and foster curiosity, courage, collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement. Oversee the eGRC helpdesk to maintain responsive support and turn recurring pain points into improvements.

Who You Are

You're an enterprise transformation leader with 10+ years of progressive leadership across risk, compliance, controls, technology, product, or related disciplines, and a record of delivering complex change in a regulated organization.
You bring deep operational risk judgment. You understand how frameworks, assessments, controls, issues, losses, data, and regulatory expectations connect, and translate that expertise into practical choices without unnecessary complexity.
You champion trusted data and high-performing partnerships. You have established data ownership, standards, quality, lineage, and remediation practices, and can challenge and inspire strategic technology vendors to improve performance, innovation, risk management, and value.
You're a visionary, customer-focused product leader who reimagines risk programs through AI, automation, data, and human-centred design. You turn complex user, business, and regulatory needs into a clear roadmap and align stakeholders around measurable outcomes.
You have a record of delivering transformation at scale, leading multi-year initiatives from business case and design through implementation, integration, operating model change, adoption, and continuous improvement, with measurable results.
You're an influential executive partner and storyteller who builds trust across boundaries, simplifies complex risk and technology choices, and communicates with the clarity needed to influence executives, governance committees, and delivery teams.
You're technically fluent and future-focused. You engage credibly with engineering, architecture, data, automation, design, security, and risk teams; understand platforms, integrations, analytics, generative and agentic AI, and responsible AI controls; and scale promising use cases into governed enterprise capabilities.
You turn ambiguity into momentum by framing problems, testing hypotheses, learning quickly, and adapting as user needs, technology, risk, and regulatory expectations evolve—without losing sight of the long-term ambition.
You're an inspiring people leader who creates purpose and clarity, develops strong talent, empowers sound decisions, and enables teams to deliver ambitious outcomes together.
You bring relevant education and professional credibility. An undergraduate or advanced degree in Business, Risk Management, Technology, Finance, or a related field is preferred; relevant risk, audit, technology, product, or project management designations are an asset.
Values matter to you. You bring your real self to work, and you live our values - trust, teamwork, and accountability.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.
Subject to plan and program terms and conditions

What You Need To Know

CIBC is committed to creating an inclusive environment where all team members and clients feel like they belong. We seek applicants with a wide range of abilities and we provide an accessible candidate experience. If you need accommodation, please contact Mailbox.careers-carrieres@cibc.com
CIBC is committed to clarity in our hiring process. All roles posted are opportunities we’re actively recruiting for, unless stated otherwise.
You need to be legally eligible to work at the location(s) specified above and, where applicable, must have a valid work or study permit.
We may ask you to complete an attribute-based assessment and other skills test (such as simulation, coding, French proficiency).
We use artificial intelligence tools during the recruitment process. Our goal for the application process is to get to know more about you, all that you have to offer, and give you the opportunity to learn more about us.

jobs.title: Director, Product Automation
jobs.description:
Job Description:

ICUC is the global leader in Social Media solutions for over 20 years. To date, the ICUC team consists of over 350 people, in over 35 countries, covering 50 languages around the clock. In an environment where the only constant is change, we create common ground between brands and audiences across communities and social media. Fueled by a unique culture built in and around meritocracy, we bring the passion, the know-how and the balance necessary to maintain the charted course we set for ourselves: to be the best, we employ the best. Are you ready to be part of the ICUC team?

The Role

ICUC is creating a new leadership role to own our automation and AI strategy across the business. This is a product and innovation mandate, not a workforce-efficiency one: the Director, Product Automation is responsible for how AI and automation get built into the actual work we do for clients — community management, strategy, insights, monitoring, and social listening, so our teams can work faster, with more precision, and with sharper focus on the client.

This is a founding, leadership-level position. You'll set the vision and build the function from the ground up, working closely across leadership to make sure ICUC's AI and automation strategy is as strong internally as it is in how we tell that story to the market.

What You'll Be Doing

Automation & AI Strategy

Own ICUC's automation and AI strategy as it applies to our products and service delivery
Evaluate, pilot, and select tools and technologies that make our core services - community management, strategy, insights, monitoring, and social listening - faster, more precise, and more scalable, without compromising the quality clients expect.
Define a standardized, scalable automation blueprint for ICUC's service offerings, rather than one-off, client-by-client fixes.
Build the reporting infrastructure needed to measure automation impact including efficiency gains, quality, and margin — across our platform ecosystem.
Bring a product mindset to this work: treat automation and AI capability as a product to be designed, tested, and iterated, not a back-office project.

Cross-Functional Leadership

Partner closely with Operations, Product Marketing and Growth to translate our internal automation and AI capability into external go-to-market positioning and messaging.
Collaborate with Marketing to align messaging with ICUC's broader brand and content strategy.
Work across delivery, operations, and client success teams to ensure new tools and workflows are adopted in practice, not just approved in theory.

Organizational Leadership

Represent automation and AI strategy at the leadership table, helping shape how ICUC positions itself against AI-native competitors and evolving client expectations.
Build and champion a clear, company-wide narrative for what "AI-enabled, human-powered" means at ICUC, internally and externally.
Mentor and influence teams across the business to build automation literacy and confidence, without a large direct team of your own at the outset.

What You Bring To The Table

Proven experience building or scaling a product, automation, or AI/technology strategy function, ideally within a services, agency, or martech environment.
A track record of taking automation or AI capability from concept to measurable operational impact.
Strong cross-functional collaboration skills; comfortable partnering with marketing, delivery, and executive stakeholders who may have different priorities.
Familiarity with social media, community management, or social listening platforms is a strong asset.
Experience navigating the reporting and data limitations of enterprise martech platforms and building workarounds or systems to close those gaps.
A genuine product-innovation mindset: curious about tools and technology but always tying it back to what makes the client experience better.
Comfortable operating as a founding leader in a new function - able to build structure and process without waiting for someone else to define it.

. Actual salary within the salary range will be based on a variety of factors including relevant experience, knowledge, and skills. A range of medical, dental, RRSP, paid time off, and/or other benefits also are available to all permanent employees.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
In this Director of Finance position - this is a rare opportunity to join a local BC-based company that is scaling up! A fast-growing company now at 8 million gross revenue (with stretch goals this year to reach 10 million) in the business services insurance space that is making customers' lives easier with compassion and data.

You will work alongside the CEO and leadership team - your voice will be heard, and your inputs can be implemented in days, not years.If you are keen on joining a local and growing company, where ideas are heard and implemented, and prides itself on daily improvement - this is for you!

Top level:

The Director of Finance is a senior financial leader responsible for overseeing the organization’s financial operations, planning, reporting, and strategic financial management. To be clear, you are the sole individual in finance on the leadership team - and will have the opportunity to build around when the timing is right.

This role provides financial insight and leadership to executive management while ensuring the accuracy, integrity, and effectiveness of the company’s financial processes.
The Director of Finance will lead budgeting and forecasting, financial reporting, cash flow management, financial analysis, internal controls, and long-term financial planning. The successful candidate will be a strategic business partner who can translate financial data into actionable recommendations and help drive sustainable growth and profitability.

Key Responsibilities:

Financial Leadership & Strategy

Develop and execute financial strategies aligned with the organization’s overall business objectives.
Serve as a trusted financial advisor to the CEO, executive leadership team, and other senior stakeholders.
Provide financial analysis, insights, and recommendations to support strategic and operational decision-making.
Evaluate business performance, profitability, investments, and growth opportunities.
Establish financial policies, processes, controls, and performance standards.

Budgeting & Forecasting

Lead the annual budgeting and planning process.
Develop financial forecasts and regularly update projections based on business performance and market conditions.
Monitor actual results against budgets and forecasts, identifying trends, risks, and opportunities.
Partner with department leaders to improve financial accountability and resource allocation.

Financial Reporting & Analysis

Oversee timely and accurate monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting.
Completion of all T2s
Prepare management reports, dashboards, and financial presentations for senior leadership and, where applicable, the Board of Directors.
Analyze revenue, expenses, margins, cash flow, working capital, and key performance indicators.
Develop meaningful financial metrics to measure business performance.

Accounting & Controls

Oversee accounting operations, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, general ledger, payroll, and financial close processes.
Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, tax requirements, and regulatory obligations.
Maintain strong internal controls and financial governance.
Coordinate with external auditors, tax advisors, banking partners, and other financial service providers.

Cash Flow & Risk Management

Manage cash flow forecasting and liquidity planning.
Monitor working capital and optimize cash management.
Identify financial, operational, and business risks and recommend appropriate mitigation strategies.
Support insurance, banking, financing, and other financial arrangements as required.

Team Leadership

Lead, mentor, and develop the finance and accounting team.
Establish clear goals, performance expectations, and professional development plans.
Promote a culture of accountability, accuracy, continuous improvement, and business partnership.
Evaluate and improve finance systems, processes, and technology.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.
CPA, CFA, MBA, or other relevant professional designation is an asset.
5+ years of progressive experience in finance, accounting, financial planning and analysis, or a related discipline.
Demonstrated experience leading budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and strategic analysis.
Strong understanding of accounting principles, financial controls, and business finance.
Experience managing and developing finance professionals.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
Excellent communication and presentation abilities.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and financial reporting/ERP systems.

Preferred Experience

Experience in a senior finance leadership role within a growing or complex organization.
Experience with financial systems implementation, process improvement, and automation.
Strong commercial and operational understanding, with the ability to connect financial performance to business strategy.
Experience managing external auditors, tax advisors, lenders, and other external stakeholders.

Financials:

Full time - full time in office with option for hybrid after first 3 months
Pay Range - 120k to 170k
Comprehensive benefits program - including dental care, vision care, and paid time off
Annual bonus based on profitability on business

jobs.title: Director of Finance And Operations
jobs.description:
Who We Are? 

Driven by a vision to eliminate poverty in our community, Bissell Centre’s data-driven approach is rooted in a deep belief in the dignity, strength, and potential of every individual. Through compassion, optimism, and strong relationships, our prevention and stabilization strategy and programs empower people by supporting our community to secure housing and build sustainable livelihoods. Our community comes from all walks of life, and so does our team—united by a shared commitment to create real, lasting change. By joining Bissell Centre, you will become part of a fast-paced and dedicated team that works together to realize our vision.  

Currently, Bissell Centre is looking for a Director, Finance & Operations
to join our dedicated Administration team
as we journey with the Community towards an elimination of poverty. If you’re ready to bring your heart to a fast-paced, collaborative environment, join us in making an impact in our community.  

How You’ll Make an Impact? 

Reporting to the Co-CEO, the Director, Finance & Operations
is a key member of the leadership team, overseeing Bissell Centre’s financial stewardship, operational infrastructure, facilities, and risk management. This role provides strategic oversight for an annual operating budget of approximately $20M, ensuring fiscal integrity, compliance, operational excellence, and environmental sustainability across all sites. 
Executive & Board Advisory: Partner directly with the Executive Team and the Finance, Audit and Risk Management (FARM) Committee on strategic objectives, trend evaluation, and policy recommendations. Lead financial agenda items at quarterly FARM Committee meetings, coordinate external auditor selection, and serve on call for Board meetings as required. 
Accounting Integrity & Compliance: Provide overall fiscal stewardship for an annual operating budget of approximately $20M. Ensure all transactions, journal entries, accounts, and financial statements fully comply with Board policies, funder/donor designations, legal requirements, GAAP, and Accounting Standards for Not-for-Profit Organizations (ASNPO).  
Site & Equipment Maintenance: Oversee operations, physical safety, and preventative maintenance across all owned and leased sites, including Moonlight Bay Camp at Wabamun Lake. Ensure machinery, electrical/mechanical systems, and vehicles meet health and safety standards through regular building inspections. 
Vendor & Contract Management: Oversee agency-wide procurement to drive cost savings. Negotiate vendor contracts, manage contractor relationships and project deadlines, and cultivate local supplier partnerships to secure discounts or donations.

jobs.title: Director of Financial Planning and Analysis
jobs.description:
Management Resources is partnering with a large, complex organization within the mining and natural resources sector seeking an experienced Director, FP&A to provide senior-level support through a critical planning and budgeting period. This is an immediate-start, 3-month contract with strong potential for extension, offering a hybrid work model with three days per week onsite in downtown Vancouver.

This individual will take a lead role in consolidated long-range planning and the annual budgeting process, providing an enterprise-wide view of financial performance, capital requirements, cash flow, liquidity and financing capacity. The role will work closely with senior finance and operational leaders across multiple regions and present key insights and recommendations to executive leadership.

Key Responsibilities
Lead the consolidated 3-year long-range planning process, including financial performance, cash flow, capital requirements, liquidity and financing capacity.
Lead the development and consolidation of the 2027 Annual Budget, integrating plans across North America, Latin America and Enterprise Operations.
Review regional and functional plans at the consolidated level to ensure alignment with overall corporate and financial objectives.
Evaluate financial assumptions and challenge inputs, identifying key risks, opportunities and areas requiring further analysis.
Partner closely with Finance Business Partners and operational leadership across the organization.
Assess capital constraints, available cash and overall funding capacity to support the organization's long-term plan.
Prepare and present forward-looking financial analysis, scenarios, recommendations and executive-level materials.
Perform sensitivity analysis across earnings, cash flow, capital investment, liquidity, commodity pricing and other key business drivers.
Provide senior leadership with a holistic view of the organization's financial outlook and strategic capital priorities.

Ideal Background
Extensive senior-level FP&A, corporate planning and financial analysis experience.
Strong experience working at the consolidated enterprise level within a large, complex organization, ideally $1B+ in revenue.
Mining or natural resources experience strongly preferred; candidates from similarly complex, capital-intensive industries may also be considered.
Significant experience with long-range planning, annual budgeting, cash flow, liquidity and capital planning.
Comfortable challenging assumptions and partnering with senior finance and operational stakeholders.
Strong executive communication skills with experience preparing materials and presenting insights to senior leadership.
Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced environment during a critical budgeting and planning cycle.

If you are an experienced accounting and financial professional, please apply to Robert Half Management Resources today. Please contact our Vancouver office and submit your resume noting "Director, FP&A" in the subject line. Please quote Job number 05060-0013516613 in all correspondence.

You must currently live in Vancouver, and be legally authorized to work in Canada.
